SSE Composite Today: Shanghai Falls to 3,634.35 as AI Hardware Slumps and ChiNext Drops 3.32% Amid Nvidia's Turmoil
sum: Mainland Chinese stocks opened higher but slid in the afternoon as optical-module and circuit-board makers sold off on Nvidia’s leadership turmoil, while banks hit record highs and kept the Shanghai benchmark well ahead of Shenzhen.

The Shanghai Composite Index closed at 3,634.35 points on Friday 13 November 2026, down 21.48 points or 0.59%. It was the index’s second straight decline after a 0.67% fall to 3,655.83 on Thursday, and it left the benchmark back below its five-day and ten-day moving averages. The session range ran from 3,623.84 to 3,669.44.

The headline loss understates the damage across the wider market. The Shenzhen Component Index fell 2.05% to 10,968.79, the growth-focused ChiNext Index slid 3.32% to 2,426.08, the STAR 50 lost 2.30% to 1,279.66 and the blue-chip CSI 300 eased 0.68% to 4,016.29. More than 4,700 stocks declined against roughly 750 that rose, and combined Shanghai and Shenzhen turnover shrank to about 1.66 trillion yuan, around 276 billion yuan less than on Thursday.

A-shares opened higher and the Shanghai Composite traded in positive territory through the morning, briefly rising about 0.2% towards 3,663. The tone changed sharply after the lunch break, when selling hit the computing-hardware complex and the index fell almost 1% at its worst before trimming losses into the close.

The dominant story of the session was the abrupt exit of Jensen Huang, the co-founder who had led Nvidia since 1993. The company said on Thursday that he had stepped down as president, chief executive and board member with immediate effect, following reports of multiple affairs, including one with a woman US intelligence suspects of spying for China. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO, Harvey C. Jones becomes the company’s first independent chairman, and Nvidia is due to report quarterly results next week. Nvidia shares opened as much as 14% lower on Thursday before closing down 4.34%, and extended losses on Friday after HSBC downgraded the stock.

Chinese suppliers of optical modules, printed circuit boards and electronic components have been among the biggest beneficiaries of US AI data-centre spending, so the uncertainty around Nvidia’s strategy hit them hardest.

China Stock Themes Get Shaken Up: Domestic Computing-Power Chain Surges Against the Tide as Robotics, AI Comic-Drama Plays Get Slaughtered
sum: Chinese stocks rallied intraday on Thursday (the 12th) before running into selling pressure, with the ChiNext Index ending the session down more than 2% as the gap between bulls and bears widened markedly during the day. The index remains in a volatile base-building phase, with capital highly concentrated and structural divergence the defining feature of this leg of the market. Against a backdrop of rapid theme rotation, the domestic computing-power chain broke out against the tide to become one of the few bright spots, while previously strong robotics, physical AI and AI comic-drama plays all sold off sharply.

The domestic computing-power chain clearly outperformed the overseas supply chain on Thursday. Tianpu Co. locked in a third consecutive daily limit-up, Cambricon (688256.SS) climbed more than 8% intraday, and Enflame Technology (688691.SS) surged over 13% to set a record high since its listing. MetaX (688802.SS) and Moore Threads (688795.SS) rose in tandem, creating a valuation-comparison effect across the entire supply chain.

In its latest report, China Merchants Securities (600999.SS) concluded that the current correction in the semiconductor group stems from two forces: profit-taking on high-level positions and a temporary disturbance in market risk appetite. It is not a weakening of industry fundamentals, and the sector's medium- to long-term upward trend remains intact. The brokerage also expects the pace of domestic delivery and volume ramp-up of AI computing chips to accelerate further.

The spillover effect of computing-power demand is also starting to show up in other sub-sectors. Market analysis suggests that AI computing demand will extend into mature-process areas such as analog chips and power components, lifting those segments out of their troughs. At the same time, continued capacity expansion and advancing process nodes at Chinese memory-chip and advanced-logic production lines will further drive the domestic substitution of semiconductor equipment and core components, while upstream materials demand is expected to rise steadily alongside capacity ramp-ups and product-line expansion. In other words, the growth thesis of semiconductor self-sufficiency has not been broken.

China's ChiNext Index Surges Over 3% in a Single Day as Computing-Power Hardware Stocks Rally on Heavy Volume; Robotics and AI Comic-Drama Themes Stay Hot
sum: Mainland Chinese stocks rose in choppy trade on Wednesday (Nov. 11), with the ChiNext Index gaining more than 3% in a single day on heavier turnover, as short-term market sentiment saw a phase-specific repair. The computing-power hardware group staged a strong rebound after a prolonged low-volume consolidation, becoming the main force lifting the market, while the robotics and AI comic-drama themes remained repeatedly active.

The sustainability of the move will be the key focus for the near term. Market participants noted that if fresh capital fails to follow through with sufficient force, the index could spike into resistance and then pull back, and the overall picture should still be viewed as a choppy bottom-building structure rather than a trend reversal.

Computing-power hardware stocks were the standout performers yesterday. Eoptolink (300502.SZ) and Zhongji Innolight (300308.SZ) both surged more than 15%, while Cambridge Technology (603083.SS), Accelink Technologies (002281.SZ) and Dongshan Precision (002384.SZ) hit their daily limits. Institutional analysts said that after a long period of low-volume consolidation, trading crowding in the group has fallen markedly, and the previously concentrated positions have largely been cleared out.

On fundamentals, third-quarter earnings delivery and capital expenditure orders from overseas cloud providers show that the industry chain's business conditions have not undergone a fundamental reversal. Industry participants believe the decline mainly reflects valuation digestion and a sentiment pullback after earlier outsized gains, and that sector valuations have returned to a relatively cost-effective range, providing conditions for a phase-specific repair.

However, most individual stocks still carry a large overhang of trapped positions, and given that computing-power hardware carries a relatively high weight in the index, any sustained rebound will still require steady, expanding volume. Market information indicates that once buying support weakens, the group is highly likely to see renewed choppy trading, and investors should still watch short-term timing.
Among theme stocks, the two hot directions of robotics and AI comic-drama continued to attract capital.

sum: On the morning of November 10, China's three major A-share indexes opened higher and then pulled back, with gains narrowing from the open. By the midday close, the Shanghai Composite was up 0.06%, the Shenzhen Component 0.76%, the ChiNext Index 1.49% and the STAR Composite Index 1.32%. Combined turnover across the Shanghai and Shenzhen markets reached CNY 96.03 billion (approximately $14.4 billion) in the half session, down CNY 4.91 billion (approximately $740 million) from the previous trading day. More than 3,800 stocks across the market advanced, pointing to a notable money-making effect.

On the board, themes rotated at a faster pace, with the humanoid robot concept emerging as the strongest main line as more than a dozen constituent stocks sealed limit-up. Among them, Zhejiang Fulai New Material recorded its third limit-up in five days, while Guangyang Bearing, Fenglong Co., Ltd. and Huapei Power each posted a second straight limit-up. Short-drama concept stocks remained active on and off, with Wintime Investment Holding up for a second consecutive session, Shanghai Film posting its second limit-up in three days, and Ciwen Media, Zhangyue Technology and Jinyi Film & Television hitting the daily limit. In edge AI, Sunsea AIoT rose for a second time in four days and Fullhan Microelectronics gained more than 14%. In the ice-and-snow economy theme, Bingshan Refrigeration & Heat Transfer Technologies notched its fifth limit-up in nine days. On the downside, the oil and gas sector weakened, with CNOOC, China Oilfield Services and other names falling.

Note: Data reflect the morning close on November 10; combined half-day turnover for the two markets was CNY 96.03 billion (approximately $14.4 billion), down CNY 4.91 billion (approximately $740 million) from the prior trading day.

On the outlook, Huachuang Securities sees three supporting factors reinforcing a year-end rebound window. First, on liquidity, improving macro and micro liquidity is driving valuation repair, and market reactions to negative news have become more muted since the U.S. midterm elections. Second, on U.S. Treasury yields, both real rates and inflation expectations have retreated, easing external financial conditions.

China A-shares pare early gains at midday: ChiNext Index up 0.56% as PCB and coal stocks hit limit-up
sum: China's three major A-share indices all surged in early trading on the 9th before pulling back, though they held onto modest gains by midday. At the lunch break, the Shanghai Composite Index was up 0.46%, the Shenzhen Component Index up 0.27% and the ChiNext Index up 0.56%, after the ChiNext had risen more than 1.5% intraday. Combined half-day turnover on the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges was about 1.01 trillion yuan (approximately $151 billion), down 111.6 billion yuan from the previous trading day, with more than 2,600 stocks in the broader market advancing.

Market activity was concentrated in two areas: electronics and cyclicals. PCB concept stocks moved higher in choppy trade, with Aoshikang (002913.SZ), Worldex (603920.SS) and Goworld (000823.SZ) hitting limit-up. The coal sector strengthened across the board, with Zhengzhou Coal Industry & Electric Power (600121.SS) and Antai Group (600408.SS) both sealing limit-up. Robotics concept stocks were also active, with Xiangming Intelligent, Taier Heavy Industry and Guangyang Bearing among those hitting limit-up. Commercial space names advanced, with China Satellite (600118.SS), Shunhao and Shengyang Technology among the gainers hitting limit-up. In the ice-and-snow economy theme, Bingshan Refrigeration and Longjiang Transport extended gains to a fourth limit-up in eight sessions.

On the downside, the solar sector opened higher but faded, becoming the main drag on the indices. Sungrow Power Supply (300274.SZ) and LONGi Green Energy (601012.SS) both fell, while Shichuang Energy dropped more than 7%.
Note: Turnover figures are combined half-day data for the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges.

Looking ahead, Guosen Securities said Chinese regulators have taken multiple measures recently to stabilize capital market confidence, and market-stabilizing forces are gradually entering and beginning to take effect. Uncertainty around the U.S. midterm elections has now been resolved, and expectations for an easing of geopolitical tensions are rising. At the same time, the tech holdings in institutional portfolios may be approaching a substantive clearing point. The brokerage judged that positive market expectations are gradually taking hold and the rebound is likely to continue.

items.t: US October Nonfarm Payrolls Surge by 165,000; Market Bets on Fed Restarting Rate Hikes in December
sum: Data released last Friday by the US Department of Labor showed that nonfarm payrolls surged by about 165,000 in October, far exceeding the market estimate of 65,000, following a prior increase of 29,000. The unemployment rate for the month fell in tandem to 4.1%. The markedly stronger-than-expected jobs report quickly changed the pricing logic in interest rate markets, with traders increasing bets that the Federal Reserve will restart rate hikes in December.

According to Jinshi Data, the dollar index strengthened sharply after the data release, eventually closing up 0.75% at 102.31. The 2-year Treasury yield, which is sensitive to the Fed's policy rate, rose 5 basis points to 4.512%, while the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed 4 basis points to 4.856%. Fed officials' subsequent remarks also leaned hawkish. Daly said she is prepared to raise rates further if needed and stressed that policy decisions require prudence, while Williams said outright that inflation is too high and has persisted for too long.

Strong employment and rising yields weighed on precious metals. Spot gold plunged during the session, falling below the $4,030 mark, and closed down 0.43% at $4,070.31 an ounce. Spot silver traded sideways, closing up 0.37% at $51.95 an ounce. In crude oil, the market weighed the outlook for the Middle East situation against the dampening effect of tightening expectations on energy demand; WTI crude closed down 0.89% at $89.46 a barrel, and Brent crude closed down 1.27% at $96.73 a barrel.

The three major US stock indexes were mixed, with the Dow down 0.46%, the S&P 500 up 0.31% and the Nasdaq up 1.09%. Most chip stocks rebounded: AMD (AMD) jumped 11.04%, Intel (INTC) rose 7.71%, Micron Technology (MU) gained 5.12%, Nvidia (NVDA) added 2.78% and Arm (ARM) rose 4.74%. The Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index rose 1.67%, with Baidu (BIDU) up 3.01% and NetEase (NTES) up 2.28%. Major European stock indexes all fell, with Germany's DAX down 2.02% and the UK's FTSE 100 down 1.01%.
In Asia-Pacific markets, Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fluctuated lower throughout the session, closing down 1.27% at 24,481.86 points, while the Hang Seng Tech Index fell 1.83%.

Guojin Securities' Mou Yiling: Blue-Chip Valuations Near Historic Lows, Three Themes to Capture Structural Opportunities in China's A-Shares
sum: From November 6 to 7, Mou Yiling, chief strategist and executive deputy director of the research institute at Guojin Securities, said in a media interview that China's A-share market has been under sustained pressure since mid-to-late September, with rising external uncertainty the core disturbance behind this round of adjustment. However, he believes that valuations of core blue-chip A-share stocks have already fallen into a historically low range, and that combined with the fundamental resilience shown in third-quarter earnings and a wave of buybacks by listed companies, the market's underlying logic remains solid.

On the sources of external risk, Mou offered two threads. The first is geopolitical and inflation pressure: US-Iran talks are progressing slowly, excessively high oil prices are raising inflation risk, and although US Treasury yields have pulled back they remain elevated, with expectations of tightening liquidity weighing broadly on valuations of global risk assets. The second is disruption to the AI industry narrative: as overseas AI tech giants, represented by large cloud providers, reported earnings one after another, and leading closed-source large-model developer Anthropic published its prospectus, market concerns about returns on AI industry investment have reignited. In addition, after the US midterm elections the Democratic Party won control of both chambers of Congress, creating a divided government between Congress and the White House, which has raised uncertainty over industrial policy expectations and further suppressed risk appetite.

In contrast to the external disturbances, the report card delivered by China's third-quarter A-share earnings shows demand-side support remains. Citing data, Mou noted that in the third quarter of 2026, cumulative year-on-year revenue growth for all A-share companies (excluding financials and real estate) reached 7.4%, up 0.2 percentage points from the second quarter.

China's Four Major A-Share Indexes Open Lower; AI Hardware Sector Leads Declines as Over 5,400 Stocks Fall
sum: On the morning of November 6, China's four major A-share indexes opened collectively lower. The Shanghai Composite Index fell 2.11%, the Shenzhen Component Index dropped 3.72%, the ChiNext Index declined 4.99%, and the STAR Composite Index slid 5.33%, with more than 5,400 stocks across the market losing ground.

On the board, AI hardware-related sectors led the declines. The CPO sector fell sharply, with TFC Communication, Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink Technology all opening more than 10% lower, while Yuanjie Technology, Robotechnik and Focuslight Technologies posted some of the steepest drops, with Zhongji Innolight down more than 12%. The components sector also weakened, with Dongshan Precision and Aohong Electronics hitting the daily limit down, Xunjiexing and Mankun Technology falling more than 10%, and Sihui Fuji, Nanya New Material and Huazheng New Material following lower.

In contrast, the insurance and banking sectors bucked the trend, while the power sector rallied intraday, with Xinneng Shares hitting the daily limit up and Nanwang Technology, Lixin Energy and Huaneng Hydropower rising in sympathy.
As of press time, overall market sentiment remained weak, with capital clearly withdrawing from AI hardware and defensive sectors receiving some support.

Shanghai Composite Climbs Nearly 1% as Beijing Weighs Fresh Stock Support After Record 12-Week Losing Streak
sum: SHANGHAI — Chinese stocks rose on Monday as investors bet on new government measures to support the market, offsetting disappointing official data showing the economy weakened in October.
The Shanghai Composite index was up 34.21 points, or 0.95%, at 3,633.23 in afternoon trading. The index had risen as much as 1.16% by the midday break.
Gains were stronger elsewhere. The Shenzhen Component index was up 2.39% at midday, while the ChiNext index of growth stocks jumped 3.28%.

The rally was driven by reports that China's central bank would meet with financial and securities regulators and major banks on Monday to study improving a relending program that helps fund share buybacks.
The meeting comes after Chinese stocks suffered a record 12-week losing streak, with the CSI 300 index recording its worst month in more than a decade in October.
Any new steps would add to stabilization efforts launched last month, which have so far failed to reverse the downturn amid weak domestic demand and concerns about AI-related earnings.
The People's Bank of China also moved to anchor short-term rates, shifting to a daily overnight repo operation at 1.25%, in a move compared to the U.S. Federal Reserve's approach.

China regulators act to support stocks after October slump, mainland media reports
sum: Chinese financial regulators are preparing to take action to stabilize the market after a sharp decline in A-shares during October, according to mainland media reports.

The reports said that the People’s Bank of China, the China Securities Regulatory Commission, and the National Financial Regulatory Administration will meet with major banks on Monday. The regulators are expected to discuss expanding capital market support tools, including optimizing special re-lending facilities for stock buybacks and share purchases.
The special re-lending facility is designed to help listed companies and major shareholders access low-cost funds to repurchase shares and bolster stock prices.
A-shares experienced a significant downturn in October, with major indices hitting new lows for the year.
The Shanghai Composite Index fell 1.44 percent to close at 3,599.00 points on the final trading day of October, dropping below the 3,600-point mark for the first time this year.

Growth and tech stocks led the slide, with the Shenzhen Component Index down 2.73 percent to 10,833.78, the ChiNext Index dropping 4.13 percent to 2,413.63, and the SSE Science and Technology Innovation Board 50 Index declining 4.66 percent to 1,421.31.

Declines were widespread across sectors, led by heavy sell-offs in tech and media shares. More than 4,600 stocks across the entire market recorded losses. Combined turnover on the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges reached 1.67 trillion yuan (HK$1.97 trillion) that day, up 117.9 billion yuan from the previous session.
